subject: Animation
title: Sequelitis: The Pressure to Repeat Success
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Sequelitis: The Pressure to Repeat Success.

hook.text: After Disney acquired Pixar, the pressure to produce sequels increased dramatically.

buildup.text: Cars 2, Monsters University, and Finding Dory were all sequels that divided fans and critics.

discovery.text: Sequels are safer financial bets. Studios can predict returns on known characters more easily.

twist.text: Pixar's best sequels — Toy Story 3 and Inside Out 2 — prove sequels can match or surpass originals.

climax.text: The sequel debate forces Pixar to balance creative ambition with the business demands of a public company.

punchline.text: The hardest story to tell is the one that follows a masterpiece.

quiz.question: Why did sequel production increase after Disney acquired Pixar?
options: Pixar ran out of original ideas
Sequels are safer financial bets because studios can predict returns on known characters
Disney fans demanded sequels through online petitions
